content.text:
The campaign ran 27 June to 9 July. It finished under budget and reported 27 completed installs through "Wallet installed".

## Recap

| | Total |
|---|---|
| Spend | **$362.85** of the $400.00 budget (about $37 unspent) |
| Impressions | **350,583** |
| Link clicks | **188** |
| "Wallet installed" installs | **27** (22 after a post click, 5 after viewing a post only) |

Cost per reported install came to about $13.44. The figures cover 27 June 00:00 to 9 July 23:59 UK time, and the last hours of attribution may still be updating.

**What I set up:** One campaign with two ad groups, both optimised for the "Wallet installed" event. Both were UK-only and limited to iOS and Android, so desktop and tablet were excluded. Only your five approved posts ran.
- **Ad group A:** posts 2202190061369539840 and 2202552449234154346, the plain "scan and pay, no monthly fee" posts.
- **Ad group B:** posts 2202371255301263080, 2202733643170090864 and 2202914837102979029, the receipt-muddle, "£0 to download" and deadline posts.

**What worked:**
- **Ad group B did better.** In the final stretch, 3–9 July, it got 58 link clicks against 40 for A, and 9 installs against 7. That was on slightly more spend ($90.87 against $83.34).
- **Receipt-muddle post (…263080).** It had the most link clicks in both reviews. In the 30 June–4 July window it had 17 clicks and 3 installs, the best of the five posts.
- **Deadline post (…029).** It was also a strong clicker, with 14 clicks in the same window.
- **Where I put the money:** After the first review I moved budget towards B, and I moved more after the second. B's daily budget went from $14 to $17 and then to $23, and A's went from $14 to $11 and back to $14.
- **What I left alone:** Install counts are small, so I didn't pause any post. The gaps between posts could be partly chance.

Nothing is still running. Both ad groups had end times of 9 July 23:00 UTC (midnight UK time), so no spend will continue after the flight.
